evidence.definition: Male population is the percentage of the population that is male. Population is based on the de facto definition of population, which counts all residents regardless of legal status or citizenship.
evidence.source_organization:
World Population Prospects, United Nations (UN), publisher: UN Population Division;
Staff estimates, World Bank (WB), note: World Bank staff estimates based on age/sex distributions of United Nations Population Division's World Population Prospects: 2022 Revision
evidence.universe: mapped countries and territories with data

claims.text: Qatar is 71.1% male. In Russia, males make up just 46.4%.
Qatar has the world's highest male share. The global median is 49.6%.
The count includes all residents regardless of legal status or citizenship.
claims.support: Population is based on the de facto definition of population, which counts all residents regardless of legal status or citizenship.

claims.text: Across the Gulf, UAE is 63.8% male, and Kuwait is 61.1%.
Eastern Europe has some of the lowest shares: Ukraine is 46.5%, Armenia 46.4%, and Moldova 46%.
Near the global center, the USA is 50.2% male.
